paper_title: Constraining Axion-Like Particles with HAWC Observations of TeV Blazars
notes: Paper constrains ALP-photon coupling via TeV gamma-ray observations of distant blazars using HAWC and complementary ACT data (VERITAS, MAGIC, H.E.S.S.). The analysis exploits ALP-photon mixing in magnetic fields to detect excess TeV flux that would otherwise be attenuated by extragalactic background light (EBL). Main result: ALP hypothesis excluded at >3σ for g_agamma ≳ 3×10^-11 GeV^-1 for ALP masses below ~200-300 neV. The limit is mass-independent (flat) over the stated range, encoded as a horizontal line from 1 neV to 300 neV. Seven blazars used in joint likelihood analysis (MAGIC J2001+435 and PKS 1222+216 excluded due to flaring states). Limits are competitive with or better than leading terrestrial and astrophysical constraints in this mass range. No local DM density assumption applies (astrophysical/cosmological bound, not haloscope).
